question.text: What will be Mexico's forecasted meat consumption for 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the forecasted combined domestic consumption of meat (beef and veal, chicken, and swine) for Mexico in 2027 (measured in 1,000 metric tonnes carcass-weight equivalent), according to USDA Foreign Agricultural Service's [market and trade data](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/app/index.html#/app/advQuery).
question.fine_print:
To get the resolution value:

* Select all of "Meat, Beaf and Veal", "Meat, Chicken", and "Meat, Swine" from *Commodities*
* Click *Summarize* below
* Select "Domestic Consumption" from *Attributes*
* Select "Mexico" from *Countries*
* Select "2027" from *Market Years*
* Click *Run Query*

The question will resolve according to the first available forecast for 2027.

If the USDA Foreign Agricultural Service ceases to record data on Mexico's forecasted meat consumption, another suitable credible source may be used to resolve this question.

research:
## Mexico's 2027 meat consumption forecast in USDA data: research notes

**Main finding:** USDA's first forecast for 2027 looks like it has already been published, in the October 9, 2026 data release. My best reconstruction of the total is about **10,726 thousand MT**. Only the pork figure is independently confirmed; the beef and chicken figures come from search-tool readings of the report, which I could not open directly (details under 1).

### 1. Resolution source
- I could not query the PSD Online app itself, because it is a JavaScript application. The main companion report, the FAS "Livestock and Poultry: World Markets and Trade" circular, is a PDF I could not read: the fetch tool returned unreadable compressed binary (metadata creation date 2026-10-09). The fas.usda.gov copy returned a 403 error. [circular](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/circulars/livestock_poultry.pdf)
- 2026-10-09: In past years, the October circular and PSD update carried the first forecasts for the following year for major countries, including Mexico. This release is therefore probably the "first available forecast for 2027". [Meatingplace, 2026-10-14](https://meatingplace.com/daily-livestock-report-usda-forecasts-higher-global-chicken-production-flat-beef-and-pork-markets/)
- 2026-10 circular, as read by the search tool. These figures are **unverified**, since the tool flagged its own table mapping as inference:
  - Beef and veal 2027: **2,275** (2026: 2,305)
  - Pork 2027: **3,005** (2026: 2,920)
  - Chicken 2027: **5,446**
  - **Implied total: about 10,726 thousand MT.** [circular](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/circulars/livestock_poultry.pdf)
- Cross-check on pork, 2026-10-28: 3tres3 reports USDA's 2027 Mexico pork production at 1.49 Mt (+3.1%), imports at 1.76 Mt (+3.5%) and exports at 240k MT (+9.1%). Production plus imports minus exports gives about 3.01 Mt, which matches 3,005. [3tres3](https://www.3tres3.com/en/latest_swine_news/global-swine-production-usdas-initial-estimates-for-2027_22955/)
- Cross-check on chicken, 2026-08-13: the FAS Mexico Poultry Annual (MX2026-0041, the in-country attaché's forecast) puts 2027 chicken consumption at 5.5 MMT (+3%), with production at 4.4 MMT (+2%) and imports at 1.1 MMT (+4%). This is consistent with 5,446. [search summary of GAIN](https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/05/mexicos-chicken-demand-set-to-rise-3-as-world-cup-fever-hits)
- Beef context: the circular says domestic cattle supplies in Mexico have increased, cutting beef import demand, with 2027 imports forecast about 5% lower and Mexico's beef exports up 7.5%. A lower 2027 beef consumption figure is plausible on that basis. [Meatingplace](https://meatingplace.com/daily-livestock-report-usda-forecasts-higher-global-chicken-production-flat-beef-and-pork-markets/)

### 2. Current status
- If the October 2026 figures are what the question treats as the "first available forecast", the outcome is effectively settled at about 10,726. I could not confirm the exact beef and chicken numbers myself.
- Risk: PSD data are revised in the January and April 2027 updates. If the resolver simply runs the query around May 1, 2027, it may show revised values rather than the October 2026 ones.
- The question's background table shows 2026 beef at 2,320 and pork at 2,955. The October circular reportedly shows 2,305 and 2,920, so values do shift between releases.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-28: 3tres3 reports USDA's first 2027 pork estimates. Mexico's pork production and imports both rise. [3tres3](https://www.3tres3.com/en/latest_swine_news/global-swine-production-usdas-initial-estimates-for-2027_22955/)
- 2026-10-26: A farmdoc daily analysis argues that cattle held in Mexico because of the New World screwworm border closure mean more Mexican beef production and net exports. [farmdoc](https://farmdocdaily.illinois.edu/?p=43232)
- 2026-10-14: Meatingplace covers the October circular: Mexico's beef exports +7.5% and pork exports +9.1% in 2027. [Meatingplace](https://meatingplace.com/daily-livestock-report-usda-forecasts-higher-global-chicken-production-flat-beef-and-pork-markets/)
- 2026-08-24: The FAS Mexico Livestock Annual (MX2026-0040) projects 2027 beef output roughly steady and pork slaughter up about 3%. [GAIN](https://www.fas.usda.gov/data/gain/2026/08/mexico-livestock-and-products-annual)
- 2026-11-10: Moody's raises Mexico's GDP growth forecast to 2.1% for 2027, which supports demand. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/10/moodys-eleva-al-21-su-prevision-de-crecimiento-para-mexico-en-2027/)

### 4. Base rates
- Year-on-year changes in the question's PSD totals: 2021 +355, 2022 +321, 2023 +397, 2024 +306, 2025 +335, 2026 +416. Mean about +355, range +306 to +416, roughly 3.3 to 4.2% a year.
- Adding that trend to 10,601 gives about 10,900 to 11,020. The reconstructed 10,726 is only about +125 over the background's 2026 total. It is about +160 over the October-revised 2026 total (2,305 + 2,920 + roughly 5,400). The smaller step comes from the beef decline.
- First forecasts versus later revisions: as noted under 2, the 2026 values moved by -15 for beef and -35 for pork between releases, so revisions of tens of thousands of MT are typical.
- Seasonality: not relevant, since this is an annual forecast series.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on this question. The Kalshi and Polymarket markets supplied are unrelated: Mexico GDP, tariffs, elections and weather.
- The FAS attaché (GAIN) forecasts for 2027 are chicken about 5.5 MMT, pork production +3% and beef steady. These are expert inputs that USDA's official numbers usually stay close to.
- ERS long-term projections (to 2033) show steady growth in per-capita consumption. [ERS](https://www.ers.usda.gov/amber-waves/2024/august/meat-consumption-in-mexico-led-by-poultry-will-continue-rising-over-next-decade-usda-projections-show)

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Monthly WASDE reports (December 2026 through April 2027), though these cover mainly the US.
- PSD/circular updates in **January 2027** and **April 2027**, which would revise Mexico's 2027 figures (relevant if the resolver doesn't use the October value).
- FAS Mexico semi-annual GAIN reports for livestock and poultry, around March 2027.
- New World screwworm developments and the reopening of US border ports to Mexican cattle (Douglas reopened in August 2026; Columbus was scheduled for October). These affect how many cattle stay in Mexico and so its beef supply.
- USMCA review and tariffs: Kalshi puts an 83% chance on a tariff rate on Mexican imports of 10% or more on January 1, 2027. This could affect US pork and chicken exports to Mexico.

## 1. Resolution source
- I couldn't load the USDA PSD query tool: the page runs on JavaScript and the report-download address returned an HTTP 500 error. The official world-markets report (PDF) has a file date of 2026-10-09, but its text is compressed and I couldn't extract any numbers. [circular](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/circulars/livestock_poultry.pdf)
- 2026-10-09: USDA's report "Livestock and Poultry: World Markets and Trade" came out, apparently with the first official 2027 forecasts by country. Secondary coverage confirms it has 2027 figures for Mexico. [Meatingplace](https://meatingplace.com/daily-livestock-report-usda-forecasts-higher-global-chicken-production-flat-beef-and-pork-markets/)

## 2. Current status
- The question is probably close to settled already. USDA puts out the first next-year meat forecasts by country each October, so the 2027 Mexico numbers should already be in PSD. You should run the query yourself to check, keeping in mind:
  - USDA updates these forecasts monthly with the WASDE report, and the January and April 2027 releases could change them.
  - "First available forecast" is unclear about whether the October value counts or a later one.
- **Pork, from USDA's October numbers as reported by pig333 on 2026-10-28:** 2027 production 1.49 million tonnes (Mt, up 3.1%), imports 1.76 Mt (up 3.5%), exports 0.24 Mt (up 9.1%). From these I calculate consumption of about 3.01 Mt. This is my own arithmetic, ignoring stock changes; USDA didn't publish a consumption figure in that coverage. [pig333](https://www.3tres3.com/en/latest_swine_news/global-swine-production-usdas-initial-estimates-for-2027_22955/)
- **Chicken, from the August 2026 report by the USDA attaché in Mexico City:** 2027 consumption up 3% to 5.5 million metric tons (MMT), production 4.4 MMT, imports 1.1 MMT. The document is marked "not official USDA data". [APEDA copy](https://agriexchange.apeda.gov.in/MarketReport/0925904062026821113922831.pdf)
- **Beef, from the same August 2026 attaché reports:** 2027 production roughly flat, imports down 5%, exports up 7.5% (the export figure is USDA's October number). That suggests beef consumption flat to slightly down from 2026's roughly 2.3 Mt. [search summary of FAS](https://www.fas.usda.gov/data/gain/2026/08/mexico-livestock-and-products-annual); [Meatingplace](https://meatingplace.com/daily-livestock-report-usda-forecasts-higher-global-chicken-production-flat-beef-and-pork-markets/)
- Adding these up gives roughly 5,500 + 3,000 + 2,250 to 2,350, so about 10,700 to 10,900 (thousand tonnes). This is my own estimate, not a published USDA total.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-11-08: Comecarne, the Mexican meat industry council, said January to September 2026 consumption rose 2.1% for chicken and 2.4% for pork, while beef fell 2.4%. It expects total 2026 meat consumption to grow only 0.8%, against more than 4% in earlier years. It projects 2027 consumer price rises of 6% for beef, 4.8% for pork and 3.3% for chicken. It also cites USDA projections for 2027 production: chicken up 0.8%, pork up 1.1%, beef down 0.2%. Comecarne's own totals are on a different basis from USDA's, for example pork at 3.75 Mt in 2025. [Mexico Solidarity](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mexico-meat-consumption/)
- 2026-11-10: Moody's raised its Mexico GDP growth forecast to 2.1% for 2027. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/10/moodys-eleva-al-21-su-prevision-de-crecimiento-para-mexico-en-2027/)
- 2026-10-19: Derrell Peel (Oklahoma State) wrote that Mexico's beef production is projected to rise in 2027. [OK Farm Report](https://www.oklahomafarmreport.com/2026/10/19/cow-calf-corner-dr-peel-global-beef-trade-update/)
- 2026-09: USDA's economic research outlook says Mexican pork imports are forecast to rise in both 2026 and 2027. [ERS LDP-M-387](https://www.ers.usda.gov/media/29662/ldp-m-387.pdf?v=86430)
- 2026-08 and 2026-09: the US border partly reopened to Mexican cattle (closed since 2025 over screwworm). The August attaché report forecasts 2027 cattle exports up 233% to 150,000 head, which would take some supply away from the domestic market. [farmdoc](https://farmdocdaily.illinois.edu/2026/10/us-mexico-cattle-trade-and-beef-markets.html)

## 4. Base rates
- USDA's total from the question's table rose every year: 8,471 (2020), 8,826, 9,147, 9,544, 9,850, 10,185, 10,601 (2026). Yearly gains ranged from 306 to 416, averaging about 355 (about 3.8%).
- Applying that trend to 2026's 10,601 gives about 10,900 to 11,000 for 2027. The 2027 signals point lower: beef is flat or down, and chicken and pork growth is about 3%.
- 2026 values have shifted between releases. The February 2026 semi-annual reports had beef at 2.31 Mt and pork at 2.9 Mt. [FAS semi-annual](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/newgainapi/api/Report/DownloadReportByFileName?fileName=Livestock+and+Products+Semi-annual_Mexico+City_Mexico_MX2026-0012.pdf)
- Seasonality doesn't apply: this is an annual forecast series. Revisions between October and the following spring have usually been under about 1 to 2% for each commodity (this is from general knowledge; I didn't verify it this session).

## 5. Other forecasts
- No prediction market covers this question. The Kalshi and Polymarket markets supplied (Mexico GDP, tariffs, elections) are related only loosely.
- Expert inputs are the USDA attaché figures (chicken 5.5 MMT in 2027) and the USDA October pork balance (about 3.0 Mt implied), both covered above.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-12-10 (approximately): the December WASDE, with possible revisions to Mexico's figures.
- 2027-01 (approximately, with WASDE): the next "Livestock and Poultry: World Markets and Trade" report, which updates country forecasts.
- 2027-02 to 2027-03: the attaché's semi-annual reports on Mexico's livestock and poultry.
- 2027-04 (approximately): the April world-markets report, which could matter if resolution uses the value shown at check time.
- Risks that could move the numbers: screwworm-related cattle trade, US tariffs on Mexican goods (Kalshi gives 83% for a rate of 10% or more on 2027-01-01), and the peso and household incomes.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The forecast window closes on 2026-12-31, and the question resolves around 2027-05-01. The first 2027 forecast appears to have been published already in the October 9, 2026 PSD release. The January and April 2027 PSD updates could revise it before the resolver runs the query.

(b) The background table puts the 2026 total at 10,601 (beef 2,320, chicken 5,326, pork 2,955). The October 2026 release reportedly revised 2026 to about 10,625 (beef 2,305, pork 2,920, chicken about 5,400). The reconstructed first 2027 forecast from that release is:
- Beef: 2,275
- Pork: 3,005
- Chicken: 5,446
- Total: about 10,726

(c) If nothing changes, the resolution is about 10,726. The pork figure is confirmed by 3tres3 production, import and export data. Chicken matches the GAIN attaché's 5.5 MMT. The beef figure is unverified but fits the expected lower imports and higher exports.

(d) Continuing the historical trend (+306 to +416 a year) from 10,601 would give 10,900 to 11,020. The beef decline in the October forecast breaks that pattern, so the trend is a weak guide here.

(e) Revisions between PSD releases are typically tens of thousands of MT per commodity. The 2026 values moved by -15 for beef and -35 for pork. Combined revisions by April could plausibly reach ±50 to 150.

(f) The experts' expectations line up with the reconstructed figure:
- The GAIN attaché forecasts chicken at about 5.5 MMT, pork production up about 3% and beef steady.
- USDA's official reported figures sum to about 10,726.
- No markets cover this quantity.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: the search tool misread the beef or chicken numbers, or the April revision cuts chicken imports and beef because of tariffs, a peso shock or a screwworm-related cattle export surge. The total could fall to around 10,450 to 10,550.
- High: the chicken figure was actually higher (for example about 5,550), or revisions raise imports. The total could reach about 10,900 to 11,000 or more.

(b) Latest known value: the background table gives 10,601 for 2026. According to the research, the October 2026 release reconstructs 2027 as roughly 10,726 (beef 2,275, pork 3,005, chicken 5,446). Only the pork figure is cross-checked, by 3tres3 using production plus imports minus exports. The beef and chicken figures are unverified readings by the search tool.

(c) If nothing changed: about 10,726.

(d) If the trend continued: the historical +355 per year applied to 10,601 gives about 10,950. However, the specific news points lower for beef: cattle are being retained in Mexico, lowering import demand and raising exports. That fits the smaller step in the reconstruction.

(e) Historical variation: between releases, figures for a given commodity are revised by tens of thousands of MT. For example, the 2026 values moved by -15 for beef and -35 for pork. Totals typically shift by about 50 to 100 between releases. There is also some risk that the beef and chicken readings are simply wrong, perhaps by 50 to 100 each.

(f) Expert expectations: the FAS attaché forecasts chicken consumption at about 5.5 MMT, steady beef and pork up about 3%. These are consistent with about 10,700 to 10,800. There are no relevant prediction markets.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
